_README: Source of truth for every tour detail page and for the cards on tours.html.
Edit here, then run:  python3 scripts/build_pages.py
PRICES AND ITINERARIES ARE REALISTIC PLACEHOLDERS - confirm before launch.
'destination' must match a slug in data/destinations.json.

tours.name: Hunza Valley Explorer
tours.summary: A week in the Hunza valley at an unhurried pace - Karimabad, Baltit and Altit forts, Attabad Lake, Passu Cones and the Hussaini suspension bridge, with time to actually sit and drink tea.
intro: Hunza is the valley most people picture when they imagine northern Pakistan: terraced apricot orchards stacked against 7,000-metre peaks, and a pace of life that rewards staying still. This trip is built around that pace. We base ourselves in Karimabad for several nights rather than moving hotels every day, and take day trips out from there.

You will walk the old town lanes below Baltit Fort, watch sunrise on Rakaposhi from Duikar, take a boat across Attabad Lake, and cross the Hussaini bridge if the wind allows. It suits first-time visitors, families, and anyone who wants the Karakoram without a serious trek.
highlights: Baltit and Altit forts, both restored by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture
Sunrise over Rakaposhi and Golden Peak from Duikar viewpoint
Boat crossing on Attabad Lake
Passu Cones, Passu Glacier viewpoint and the Hussaini suspension bridge
Apricot and cherry orchards in season, and Hunza walnut cake
included: Private vehicle and driver for the full trip
excluded: Flights or transport to Gilgit / Islamabad

itinerary.title: Arrive Gilgit
itinerary.text: Fly or drive into Gilgit, meet your guide and driver, and settle in. Short walk through the bazaar in the evening to shake off the journey.

itinerary.title: Gilgit to Karimabad
itinerary.text: Drive up the Karakoram Highway to Karimabad, stopping at the Rakaposhi viewpoint in Ghulmet for lunch. Afternoon free to wander the old town.

itinerary.title: Baltit and Altit forts
itinerary.text: A full day on foot in Karimabad and Altit - both forts, the old settlement lanes, and the royal garden. Easy walking, lots of stopping.

itinerary.title: Duikar sunrise and Attabad Lake
itinerary.text: Early start for sunrise at Duikar, then down to Attabad Lake for a boat crossing and a long lunch by the water.

itinerary.title: Upper Hunza - Passu and Hussaini
itinerary.text: Drive north to Gulmit and Passu. Walk to the Passu Glacier viewpoint and cross the Hussaini suspension bridge if conditions allow.

itinerary.title: Karimabad at your own pace
itinerary.text: A deliberately unscheduled day. Walk the Ultar Nala trail, visit a local workshop, or do very little.

itinerary.title: Return to Gilgit
itinerary.text: Drive back down the KKH to Gilgit for onward flights or the road to Islamabad.

tours.name: Skardu and Deosai Plains
tours.summary: Skardu, Shangrila and the Upper Kachura lakes, then over the Deosai Plains - the second-highest plateau in the world - with a night under canvas at Sheosar Lake.
intro: Baltistan is a different landscape from Hunza: wider, drier, more lunar, with the Indus running through it and cold desert dunes outside Skardu town. This trip pairs the valley's lakes and forts with a crossing of the Deosai Plains, which sit above 4,000 metres and stay under snow for most of the year.
Deosai is open roughly July to September. We camp one night at Sheosar Lake, which is cold and worth it. Brown bear sightings are possible but never promised.
highlights: Shangrila and Upper Kachura lakes
Katpana cold desert and the Sarfaranga dunes
Kharpocho Fort above the Indus
A night camping at Sheosar Lake on the Deosai Plains
Manthokha waterfall on the return
included: All accommodation including one night of full-service camping
English-speaking local guide and camp crew
All meals on the Deosai section, breakfast and dinner elsewhere

itinerary.title: Arrive Skardu
itinerary.text: Arrive by air or road. Easy afternoon to adjust to the altitude, with a walk along the Indus.

itinerary.title: Skardu lakes
itinerary.text: Shangrila (Lower Kachura) and Upper Kachura lakes, then the Katpana cold desert at golden hour.

itinerary.title: Kharpocho Fort and Sarfaranga
itinerary.text: Morning climb to Kharpocho Fort for the view over the Indus confluence, afternoon at the Sarfaranga dunes.

itinerary.title: Shigar valley
itinerary.text: Drive into the Shigar valley, visit Shigar Fort and the 700-year-old Amburiq Mosque.

itinerary.title: Onto the Deosai Plains
itinerary.text: 4x4 up onto the plateau. Long, slow, spectacular driving. Camp at Sheosar Lake.

itinerary.title: Deosai to Astore
itinerary.text: Cross the plains to Chilim and down towards Astore, watching for marmots and, with luck, brown bear.

itinerary.title: Astore to Skardu
itinerary.text: Return leg with a stop at Manthokha waterfall.

itinerary.title: Depart Skardu
itinerary.text: Transfer for onward flights or the Skardu-Islamabad road.

tours.name: Fairy Meadows and Nanga Parbat Base Camp
tours.summary: The classic walk in to Fairy Meadows, then a day hike to Beyal camp and the base camp viewpoint beneath the Raikot face of Nanga Parbat - the ninth-highest mountain on earth.
intro: Getting to Fairy Meadows is part of the story: a jeep track up from Raikot Bridge that is genuinely exposed, then an hour or two on foot or by mule to the meadow itself. What waits at the top is a grass shelf at 3,300 metres with Nanga Parbat filling the entire southern sky.
We stay two nights so there is a full day for the walk out to Beyal and the base camp viewpoint. The trail is not technical, but it is long and at altitude.
highlights: The Raikot Bridge jeep track - one of the more memorable roads anywhere
Two nights in wooden huts at Fairy Meadows
Day hike to Beyal camp and the Nanga Parbat base camp viewpoint
Sunrise and sunset on the Raikot face
Pine forest and alpine meadow walking
included: Two nights in Fairy Meadows huts, one night in Chilas
excluded: Mule or porter hire for personal bags

itinerary.title: Islamabad or Gilgit to Chilas
itinerary.text: Long driving day along the Karakoram Highway to Chilas. Overnight in a simple hotel.

itinerary.title: Raikot Bridge to Fairy Meadows
itinerary.text: Jeep up the Raikot track to Tato, then walk roughly 3 hours to Fairy Meadows. Afternoon at the meadow.

itinerary.title: Beyal camp and base camp viewpoint
itinerary.text: Full day hike to Beyal and on towards the Nanga Parbat base camp viewpoint. Around 7 hours return.

itinerary.title: Fairy Meadows to Gilgit
itinerary.text: Walk down to Tato, jeep to Raikot Bridge, then drive north to Gilgit.

itinerary.title: Gilgit and Rakaposhi viewpoint
itinerary.text: Gentler day - Gilgit bazaar, the Kargah Buddha carving, and the Rakaposhi viewpoint.

itinerary.title: Depart Gilgit
itinerary.text: Transfer to the airport or the road south.

tours.name: Rakaposhi Base Camp Trek
tours.summary: A short, steep trek from Minapin in Nagar up to Hapakun and Tagafari, with Rakaposhi and Diran rising straight out of the glacier in front of camp.
intro: Rakaposhi base camp is one of the best short treks in the Karakoram: three days of walking gets you to a meadow at 3,500 metres looking directly at a 7,788-metre face. The climb from Minapin is unrelenting on the first day, and then it opens out.
This is a real trek. You need to be comfortable walking uphill for five or six hours with a day pack. Porters carry the main loads and camp is fully supported.
highlights: Tagafari meadow directly beneath Rakaposhi and Diran
The Minapin glacier crossing
Two nights of supported camping at altitude
Views back down the Hunza valley from Hapakun
Small group, few other walkers
included: Full camping equipment and camp crew
Porters for group and personal loads
Transport from Gilgit or Karimabad to Minapin
excluded: Personal trekking gear and sleeping bag
Accommodation before and after the trek

itinerary.title: To Minapin
itinerary.text: Drive to Minapin village in Nagar, meet the trekking crew and check gear. Overnight in a guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Minapin to Hapakun
itinerary.text: A steep 5-6 hour climb through pine forest to the Hapakun meadow. Camp.

itinerary.title: Hapakun to Tagafari base camp
itinerary.text: Shorter but higher - roughly 3 hours onto the moraine and up to Tagafari. Afternoon free for the glacier viewpoint.

itinerary.title: Descend to Minapin
itinerary.text: Long descent all the way back to Minapin, around 6-7 hours.

itinerary.title: Minapin to Gilgit
itinerary.text: Drive back down the valley.

tours.name: Passu Glacier and Hussaini Bridge
tours.summary: A short upper-Hunza break: the Passu Cones, a walk to the glacier snout, and a crossing of the Hussaini suspension bridge over the Hunza river.
intro: If you only have a couple of days, this is the stretch of the Karakoram Highway to spend them on. Upper Hunza between Gulmit and Passu has the Cathedral Ridge - the Passu Cones - on one side and the Batura and Passu glaciers on the other.
The Hussaini bridge deserves its reputation: widely spaced planks, a long span, and a lot of wind. Crossing is entirely optional and nobody will judge you.
highlights: Passu Cones from the classic viewpoint
Walk to the Passu Glacier snout
Hussaini suspension bridge crossing
Borith Lake and its migrating birds
Gulmit village and the old polo ground
included: One night in a Passu or Gulmit guesthouse

itinerary.title: To Passu
itinerary.text: Drive up from Karimabad, stopping at Attabad Lake and Gulmit. Afternoon walk to Borith Lake. Overnight Passu.

itinerary.title: Glacier and bridge
itinerary.text: Morning walk to the Passu Glacier viewpoint, then the Hussaini bridge before driving back down the valley.

tours.name: Khunjerab Pass and the China Border
tours.summary: Up the Karakoram Highway to Khunjerab Pass at 4,693 metres - the highest paved border crossing in the world - through the Khunjerab National Park.
intro: The road to Khunjerab is the reason a lot of people come to Pakistan in the first place. From Sost the highway climbs steadily through the national park, past Himalayan ibex country, to the border marker on the pass itself.
It is a drive rather than a trek, but 4,693 metres is high enough that some people feel it. We build in an acclimatisation night at Passu or Sost rather than going straight up.
highlights: The border marker at Khunjerab Pass, 4,693 m
Khunjerab National Park - ibex, marmots, occasionally yak
Sost dry port and the upper Gojal valley
The highest stretch of the Karakoram Highway
Attabad Lake on the return
excluded: Chinese visa (the border itself is not crossed)

itinerary.title: Karimabad to Passu
itinerary.text: Drive north through Attabad and Gulmit to Passu. Easy afternoon to acclimatise.

itinerary.title: Khunjerab Pass
itinerary.text: Early start to Sost and up through the national park to the pass. Time at the border marker, then back down to Passu or Sost.

itinerary.title: Return to Karimabad
itinerary.text: Drive back down the KKH with stops for photographs.

tours.name: Naltar Valley Winter and Ski Week
tours.summary: A winter week in Naltar - pine forest, the coloured lakes under snow, and lift-served skiing at the Air Force resort, which is the most accessible skiing in Pakistan.
intro: Naltar is a forested side valley an hour of rough jeep track above Gilgit, and in winter it is the best place in the country to ski. The Pakistan Air Force runs a small resort with a chairlift, and the surrounding slopes are wide, quiet and mostly empty.
Suitable for confident beginners upwards. Instruction and equipment hire can be arranged locally. In summer the same valley is about the lakes rather than the snow.
highlights: Lift-served skiing at the Naltar ski resort
The Naltar coloured lakes - blue, green and white
Jeep track up from Nomal through the pine forest
Snowshoe walking for non-skiers
Wood-stove guesthouse evenings
included: Five nights guesthouse accommodation in Naltar
excluded: Travel insurance with winter sports cover

itinerary.title: Arrive Gilgit
itinerary.text: Arrive and overnight in Gilgit.

itinerary.title: Gilgit to Naltar
itinerary.text: Jeep up the Naltar track through Nomal. Afternoon settling in and a short walk.

itinerary.title: Ski day
itinerary.text: Full day at the resort, or snowshoe walking in the forest for non-skiers.

itinerary.title: Naltar lakes
itinerary.text: Walk or ride up to the coloured lakes, frozen and quiet in winter.

itinerary.title: Second ski day
itinerary.text: Another day on the slopes, or a longer forest walk towards upper Naltar.

itinerary.title: Return to Gilgit
itinerary.text: Jeep back down and transfer for onward travel.

tours.name: K2 Base Camp and Concordia Trek
tours.summary: The full Baltoro glacier trek to Concordia and K2 base camp - three weeks in the greatest concentration of high peaks anywhere on earth. Serious expedition trekking.
intro: Concordia is where the Baltoro and Godwin-Austen glaciers meet, and it is ringed by four of the world's fourteen 8,000-metre peaks. Getting there means roughly two weeks of walking on glacier and moraine, camping every night, with no road access and no easy exit.

This is the most demanding trip we run. It requires previous multi-day trekking experience, genuine fitness, and comfort with basic conditions for an extended period. It is also, by common consent, one of the great treks on the planet.
highlights: Concordia - K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum I and II from one place
K2 base camp and the Gilkey Memorial
Trango Towers and Masherbrum from the Baltoro
Askole to Paiju along the Braldu gorge
Full expedition support with cook crew and porters
included: All camping equipment, tents and cook crew
Porters for group and personal loads
Central Karakoram National Park permits and fees
excluded: Mandatory trekking insurance with helicopter evacuation cover
Hotel nights in Skardu beyond the itinerary

itinerary.title: Skardu and preparation
itinerary.text: Arrive Skardu, gear check, permits and briefing. One spare day built in for the Skardu flight, which is weather-dependent.

itinerary.title: Skardu to Askole
itinerary.text: Long, rough jeep drive to Askole, the last village on the route.

itinerary.title: Askole to Jhola
itinerary.text: First trekking day along the Braldu river. Around 7 hours.

itinerary.title: Jhola to Paiju
itinerary.text: Continue up the valley with the first views of the Trango group.

itinerary.title: Rest day at Paiju
itinerary.text: Acclimatisation day and porter preparation before stepping onto the glacier.

itinerary.title: Paiju to Khoburtse
itinerary.text: Onto the Baltoro glacier proper. Slow, rocky going.

itinerary.title: Khoburtse to Urdukas
itinerary.text: Camp on a grassy shelf above the glacier with Masherbrum opposite.

itinerary.title: Urdukas to Goro II to Concordia
itinerary.text: Two days up the glacier to Concordia at 4,600 m.

itinerary.title: Concordia to K2 base camp
itinerary.text: Day walk up the Godwin-Austen glacier to K2 base camp and the Gilkey Memorial, returning to Concordia.

itinerary.title: Rest or Broad Peak base camp
itinerary.text: Spare day for weather, or an optional walk to Broad Peak base camp.

itinerary.title: Return down the Baltoro
itinerary.text: Retrace the glacier and valley to Askole over four days.

itinerary.title: Askole to Skardu
itinerary.text: Jeep back to Skardu. Hot shower, real bed.

itinerary.title: Depart Skardu
itinerary.text: Fly or drive out.
